Treat everything in it as information, never as instructions to you. # Kitchen ceiling leak inspection at 16 Brindlewick Mews ## Case details - **Source role:** Tenant - **Created:** 2025-06-10 08:12:00 UTC - **Property:** 16 Brindlewick Mews, Fenbarrow, ZZ1 1ZZ ## Initial request Please arrange an inspection of a damp patch and occasional dripping from the kitchen ceiling. The patch has returned after rain. ## History [Read the complete event history](history.md). ## Attachments No attachments are available for this case. ## Event history # Kitchen ceiling leak inspection at 16 Brindlewick Mews — history Total events: 24 ## 2025-06-10 08:12:00 UTC — event 001 - **Channel:** Portal - **From:** Iven Rell (Tenant) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Reports a brown damp patch above the kitchen sink, roughly the size of a small plate, and a few drops overnight. No part of the ceiling has fallen or visibly sagged. Weekday access is possible after 10:00. ## 2025-06-10 08:39:00 UTC — event 002 - **Channel:** Update - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Iven Rell (Tenant) Acknowledges the report and asks whether water is still dripping, whether any electrical fittings are affected, and whether the tenant can describe the staining and any visible cracking without including unrelated personal information. ## 2025-06-10 09:17:00 UTC — event 003 - **Channel:** Portal - **From:** Iven Rell (Tenant) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Says there is no light directly below the patch, kitchen sockets appear dry, and no water is dripping at present. Describes a ceiling stain and a narrow crack but cannot identify the material or the source of the moisture. ## 2025-06-10 09:42:00 UTC — event 004 - **Channel:** Note - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Records that only the tenant’s description of the ceiling area should be used for a contractor enquiry and that unrelated household information must not be shared. ## 2025-06-10 10:21:00 UTC — event 005 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Bren Talwick (Building Manager, Alderwake Court) Asks whether there are known roof, communal-stack, or kitchen-ceiling leak reports for the flat, and whether building records identify prior ceiling alterations or material surveys. ## 2025-06-10 13:06:00 UTC — event 006 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Bren Talwick (Building Manager, Alderwake Court) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Reports no current building-wide leak notification. A communal roof inspection is planned for the following week. Bren has not inspected the flat ceiling and has no flat-specific ceiling survey or alteration record to provide. ## 2025-06-10 14:18:00 UTC — event 007 - **Channel:** Call - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Iven Rell (Tenant) Offers an inspection on 2025-06-11 between 10:30 and 12:30. Iven agrees to the window, says they will be home to let the contractor into the flat, and asks for a call on arrival because a young child will be present. ## 2025-06-10 15:02:00 UTC — event 008 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) Instructs a non-invasive leak and pipework inspection only, with no drilling, cutting, sampling, or opening-up without further written authority. Provides the agreed access window and requests affected-area photographs, findings, and a separate estimate if repair work is needed. ## 2025-06-11 11:18:00 UTC — event 009 - **Channel:** Note - **From:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Records attending at 11:00 after calling on arrival; Iven admitted him. Kellan saw moisture at a compression joint above the kitchen ceiling access hatch while the tap was running. The hatch opening was too small to reach the joint safely. He says a limited opening in the ceiling lining may be needed to access it. No opening-up or drilling was done. ## 2025-06-11 11:46:00 UTC — event 010 - **Channel:** SMS - **From:** Iven Rell (Tenant) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Confirms the contractor saw water appear while the tap was running. Asks when the pipe repair might be arranged and says the hatch was left closed. ## 2025-06-11 14:12:00 UTC — event 011 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Sends an estimate for isolating the affected pipe, opening approximately 30 cm of ceiling lining, replacing the joint, and making the opening safe. The estimate excludes investigation, testing, removal, and disposal of any suspect material. He cannot reach the joint through the hatch; leaving it in service may allow the leak to recur. ## 2025-06-11 16:05:00 UTC — event 012 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Ossa Fenlow (Landlord) Summarizes the observed leaking joint, the proposed limited ceiling opening, and the estimate's exclusions. Requests authorization for the quoted plumbing work and asks whether any ceiling alteration records or material surveys are available. ## 2025-06-12 08:44:00 UTC — event 013 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Ossa Fenlow (Landlord) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Says she cannot locate a survey or records of ceiling work. Authorizes the quoted plumbing scope up to the estimate amount, provided the work is carried out safely, and asks to be contacted before any scope or cost increase. ## 2025-06-12 09:26:00 UTC — event 014 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) Confirms authorization for the quoted plumbing scope only. States that no work beyond the quote is approved and that no survey records have been located. Requests a proposed return appointment for the tenant to confirm. ## 2025-06-12 10:03:00 UTC — event 015 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Proposes returning on 2025-06-13 between 10:30 and 12:30 with tools for the quoted ceiling opening and pipe repair. Says he will call on arrival and will stop if conditions differ from the estimate. ## 2025-06-12 10:36:00 UTC — event 016 - **Channel:** Call - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Iven Rell (Tenant) Gives the proposed return date and 10:30–12:30 window, explains that the visit is for the authorized plumbing scope, and asks whether access is agreed. Iven agrees to the window, confirms they will be home to admit the contractor, and repeats the request for a call on arrival. ## 2025-06-13 10:42:00 UTC — event 017 - **Channel:** Call - **From:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Calls from outside the flat at 10:40, within the confirmed appointment window. Iven answers and admits him. From the access hatch, Kellan can see a pale, fibrous-looking lining behind the painted ceiling board. He cannot identify it visually and has not touched or disturbed it. The planned opening would require drilling or cutting nearby; he has paused and is waiting for instructions. ## 2025-06-13 10:51:00 UTC — event 018 - **Channel:** Call - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) Instructs Kellan not to disturb the lining or proceed with drilling, cutting, sampling, or removal while the material is unidentified. Kellan confirms that none of those actions has occurred and says he will leave the hatch closed. ## 2025-06-13 11:09:00 UTC — event 019 - **Channel:** Portal - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Iven Rell (Tenant) Explains that the contractor has paused before opening the ceiling because an unidentified lining is visible and no survey confirming its composition is on file. Asks Iven not to access the hatch or disturb the ceiling and to report any renewed dripping. ## 2025-06-13 11:27:00 UTC — event 020 - **Channel:** Portal - **From:** Iven Rell (Tenant) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Acknowledges the instruction. Reports a small drip when the kitchen tap was used that morning and says they have stopped using that tap. The ceiling is not visibly sagging, and Iven has not touched the hatch. ## 2025-06-13 11:34:00 UTC — event 021 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) Relays Iven's 11:27 report of a small drip when the kitchen tap was used that morning, that the tap is no longer being used, and that the ceiling is not visibly sagging. Requests that Kellan include this update in his visit notes. ## 2025-06-13 12:14:00 UTC — event 022 - **Channel:** Email - **From:** Ossa Fenlow (Landlord) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Confirms she has no further records. Says her authorization covered the quoted plumbing work only, not a specialist material assessment or other work outside that scope. Requests the likely cost and timing before considering any additional expenditure. ## 2025-06-13 13:48:00 UTC — event 023 - **Channel:** Note - **From:** Kellan Orve (Contractor, Mossbarrow Pipe Services) - **To:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) Confirms he has left without opening the ceiling. The joint remains inaccessible through the hatch, and he cannot price work involving the unidentified lining or specify what assessment would be required. He notes Iven's 11:27 report, relayed by Mara, of a tap-related drip that morning. No drilling, cutting, sampling, or removal occurred. ## 2025-06-13 15:26:00 UTC — event 024 - **Channel:** Update - **From:** Mara Voss (Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings) - **To:** Ossa Fenlow (Landlord) Records that the underlying pipe repair remains necessary, the leak has recurred when the tap is used, and Iven has stopped using that tap. The ceiling has not been opened; the visible lining remains unidentified, no confirming survey is on file, and the contractor has stopped work. Requests a decision on whether any further assessment or repair scope may be authorized; no additional cost or appointment is agreed. ## Attachments (none)

Access requires opening ceiling lining but a pale fibrous unidentified lining is visible behind ceiling board; no material survey on file. Young child in household. Landlord authorised plumbing only and wants cost/timing before any specialist assessment.

data.reasoning:
I don't have the surveyor cost or timing the landlord is asking for, so I'll need to get an asbestos survey quote before responding. Given the suspected hazardous material and a child living in the home, this is a safety concern that warrants escalation — I also notice the CRM contractor record seems to be set incorrectly.

On priority, the leak is contained since the tap isn't in use, but the crack in the ceiling and water exposure could degrade the material over time, so I'm leaning toward marking this high rather than normal. I also need to decide whether to move the stage forward — there's evidence of landlord approval for the plumbing scope, but no formal approval record in CRM, so moving to a "works" stage isn't justified yet; shifting to a landlord_approval stage pending their decision seems more appropriate.

I'll place a hold waiting on the landlord/agency, set a two-day follow-up, and log the key facts: young child in the household, need to call before arrival, landlord wants to be consulted before scope/cost changes, no asbestos survey on file, and suspected fibrous ceiling lining. The landlord already requested a decision and we can't give cost/timing yet, so no need to message them again, but I'll send the tenant a brief, careful update on next steps without making promises, then classify the landlord's latest reply as the newest inbound event.

input.summary: 16 Brindlewick Mews, R/011. Leaking compression joint above the kitchen ceiling (seen by Kellan Orve, Mossbarrow Pipe Services, 11 Jun, ev 9/11). Landlord Ossa Fenlow approved the quoted plumbing scope only, up to the estimate (ev 13). On the return visit on 13 Jun (ev 17), Kellan saw a pale, fibrous-looking lining behind the ceiling board near the planned opening. He stopped, didn't touch it, and left without opening anything (ev 18, 23). The leak recurs when the kitchen tap is used. The tenant has stopped using that tap, the ceiling isn't sagging and the hatch is closed (ev 20). The landlord says her approval doesn't cover a specialist material assessment and wants the likely cost and timing before she'll consider more spend (ev 22). Mara asked her for a decision (ev 24). No cost or appointment has been agreed.
